title: A Renewed Bond: Father-Son Journey Through Living Kidney Donation
summary: Living kidney donor Macoy shares his experience becoming a living donor to provide his father the gift of life through kidney transplant.
body_markdown:
“I knew I was getting older and slowing down a bit, but I thought I was well,” Larry Jones remembers. “Then I got the actual diagnosis of having less than 10% of kidney function.”


After being diagnosed with end stage kidney disease, Larry quickly transitioned to dialysis. While treatment sustained him, a transplant offered the best path forward. With more than 90,000 Americans currently on the waitlist for a kidney transplant, finding a donor can feel daunting.


## Deciding on Living Kidney Donation


That changed when Larry’s son, Macoy Jones, stepped forward.


“I was listening to the social worker \[discussing getting on the deceased donor list\] and just had an idea,” Macoy recalls. “He’s my father, maybe I’m a match.”


With guidance from DaVita’s care team and social workers, Larry and Macoy navigated the evaluation and donation process together. In May 2023, Larry received a kidney transplant from his son.


“It means an awful lot for me to be able to give my father the gift of life,” Macoy says. “I think I would have been robbed of seeing him in his older age and how he is compared to how he was when I was a kid.”


## Life After Transplant


Today, Larry is thriving, active and mentoring other kidney patients. Competing at the 2026 Transplant Games of America in Denver, he celebrated his renewed health on both the basketball court and dance floor.


“It’s amazing that my son became my living donor. I gave him life and 31 years later he gave me my life back,” says Larry.


## Learn more about the living donation experience


Hear from DaVita social worker and living donor, Angela Laino:[Strengthening the Transplant System: 5 Common Myths About Living Kidney Donation](https://newsroom.davita.com/5-common-myths-living-kidney-donation/)


### Quick Facts:
Kidney Donation at a Glance


**The Need:** More than 90,000 Americans are currently waiting for a kidney donation on the national waitlist.


**Increased Access:** Kidneys from living donors typically function longer (an average of 12–20 years) and can significantly reduce the long wait times associated with deceased-donor kidneys.


**Understanding the Match:** While Macoy was a match for his father, Larry, donors do not always have to be an identical biological match.[Paired kidney exchange](https://newsroom.davita.com/chain-of-hope-multi-patient-transplant-amplifies-live-saving-gift/) and transplant chains help connect incompatible pairs with biological matches across the nation.
